stem: In a process, \(701\,\text{J}\) of heat is absorbed by a system and \(394\,\text{J}\) of work is done by the system. What is the change in internal energy for the process?

subtopic: Measurement of ΔU and ΔH: Calorimetry
stem:
The reaction of cyanamide, \(\text{NH}_2\text{CN}(s)\), with dioxygen was carried out in a bomb calorimeter, and \(\Delta U\) was found to be \(-742.7\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) at \(298\,\text{K}\). Calculate enthalpy change for the reaction at \(298\,\text{K}\).
\(\text{NH}_2\text{CN}(g) + \dfrac{3}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{N}_2(g) + \text{CO}_2(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\)

Calculate the number of kJ of heat necessary to raise the temperature of \(60.0\,\text{g}\) of aluminium from \(35\,^\circ\text{C}\) to \(55\,^\circ\text{C}\). Molar heat capacity of Al is \(24\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\).

subtopic: Enthalpy Change, ΔrH of a Reaction – Reaction Enthalpy
stem:
Calculate the enthalpy change on freezing of \(1.0\,\text{mol}\) of water at \(10.0\,^\circ\text{C}\) to ice at \(-10.0\,^\circ\text{C}\). \(\Delta_{fus}H = 6.03\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) at \(0\,^\circ\text{C}\).
\(C_p\,[\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)] = 75.3\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\)
\(C_p\,[\text{H}_2\text{O}(s)] = 36.8\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\)

subtopic: Enthalpies for Different Types of Reactions
stem: Enthalpy of combustion of carbon to \(\text{CO}_2\) is \(-393.5\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\). Calculate the heat released upon formation of \(35.2\,\text{g}\) of \(\text{CO}_2\) from carbon and dioxygen gas.

subtopic: Enthalpy Change, ΔrH of a Reaction – Reaction Enthalpy
stem:
Enthalpies of formation of \(\text{CO}(g)\), \(\text{CO}_2(g)\), \(\text{N}_2\text{O}(g)\) and \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)\) are \(-110\), \(-393\), \(81\) and \(9.7\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) respectively. Find the value of \(\Delta_r H\) for the reaction:
\(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g) + 3\text{CO}(g) \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O}(g) + 3\text{CO}_2(g)\)

subtopic: Enthalpy Change, ΔrH of a Reaction – Reaction Enthalpy
stem:
Given
\(\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(g)\); \(\Delta_r H^{\ominus} = -92.4\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
What is the standard enthalpy of formation of \(\text{NH}_3\) gas?

subtopic: Enthalpy Change, ΔrH of a Reaction – Reaction Enthalpy
stem:
Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of \(\text{CH}_3\text{OH}(l)\) from the following data:
\(\text{CH}_3\text{OH}(l) + \dfrac{3}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2(g) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\); \(\Delta_r H^{\ominus} = -726\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
\(\text{C}(\text{graphite}) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2(g)\); \(\Delta_c H^{\ominus} = -393\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
\(\text{H}_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\); \(\Delta_f H^{\ominus} = -286\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)

subtopic: Enthalpies for Different Types of Reactions
stem:
Calculate the enthalpy change for the process
\(\text{CCl}_4(g) \rightarrow \text{C}(g) + 4\text{Cl}(g)\)
and calculate bond enthalpy of \(\text{C}-\text{Cl}\) in \(\text{CCl}_4(g)\).
\(\Delta_{vap}H^{\ominus}(\text{CCl}_4) = 30.5\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
\(\Delta_f H^{\ominus}(\text{CCl}_4) = -135.5\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
\(\Delta_a H^{\ominus}(\text{C}) = 715.0\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), where \(\Delta_a H^{\ominus}\) is enthalpy of atomisation
\(\Delta_a H^{\ominus}(\text{Cl}_2) = 242\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
For an isolated system, \(\Delta U = 0\), what will be \(\Delta S\)?

For the reaction at \(298\,\text{K}\),
\(2\text{A} + \text{B} \rightarrow \text{C}\)
\(\Delta H = 400\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) and \(\Delta S = 0.2\,\text{kJ K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}\)
At what temperature will the reaction become spontaneous considering \(\Delta H\) and \(\Delta S\) to be constant over the temperature range.

For the reaction,
\(2\text{Cl}(g) \rightarrow \text{Cl}_2(g)\), what are the signs of \(\Delta H\) and \(\Delta S\)?

For the reaction
\(2\text{A}(g) + \text{B}(g) \rightarrow 2\text{D}(g)\)
\(\Delta U^{\ominus} = -10.5\,\text{kJ}\) and \(\Delta S^{\ominus} = -44.1\,\text{JK}^{-1}\).
Calculate \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) for the reaction, and predict whether the reaction may occur spontaneously.
The equilibrium constant for a reaction is 10. What will be the value of \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\)? \(\text{R} = 8.314\,\text{JK}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(T = 300\,\text{K}\).

subtopic: Enthalpy Change, ΔrH of a Reaction – Reaction Enthalpy
stem:
Comment on the thermodynamic stability of \(\text{NO}(g)\), given
\(\dfrac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}(g)\); \(\Delta_r H^{\ominus} = 90\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
\(\text{NO}(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}_2(g)\); \(\Delta_r H^{\ominus} = -74\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
Calculate the entropy change in surroundings when \(1.00\,\text{mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\) is formed under standard conditions. \(\Delta_f H^{\ominus} = -286\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).
